selected_scene.central_story: A raven mechanic studies live measurements while a roadster remains restrained under testing

generation.prompt:
Create ONE wide 16:9 editorial illustration of a raven mechanic monitoring a vintage roadster undergoing electronic testing in a compact, well-equipped workshop. The entire scene is constructed from cut and layered matte paper, photographed under soft, diffuse daylight.

REFERENCE IMAGES
Use Image 1 for the raven’s identity: face, eyes, beak, body proportions, feather shapes, tail, legs, toes, and composed, quietly whimsical personality.
Use Image 2 for materials and lighting: tactile matte paper, visible fibers, layered construction, restrained contact shadows, and neutral daylight.
Do not reproduce the character-sheet layout, labels, or desk-and-stopwatch scene. Create the new workshop scene described below.

MATERIALS AND LIGHTING
Use crisp hand-cut edges with occasional slight deckling, visible paper tooth and fibers, believable cardstock thickness, and broad overlapping feather and object layers. Forms can have convincing physical depth, but their construction must remain visibly cut, folded, curved, and layered paper rather than smooth molded surfaces.

Everything belongs to the same tactile paper world: the raven, clothing, car, tires, monitors, screen graphics, electronic sensors, cables, tools, furniture, and plants. Even the technological equipment should look carefully fabricated from matte paper.

Photograph the construction under soft, diffuse upper-left daylight with neutral white balance. Use restrained contact shadows to describe overlapping layers and grounded objects. Keep everything in sharp focus, with no lens distortion, dramatic lighting, or glossy reflections.

PALETTE
Use warm-neutral off-white #ECE9E2, charcoal #22272B, slate teal #2E5B60, and pale sage #B7C4B4 as the base palette. Burnt copper #C2612C provides related accents on the mechanic’s uniform, adjustment handle, wheel restraints, sensor connectors, and selected screen graphics. Small amounts of muted light gray and warm tan are allowed for recognizable mechanical trim and seat upholstery.

Keep the background neutral off-white without a yellow cast. The monitors have dark charcoal screens with subdued paper-cut graphics, not luminous displays casting colored light.

SCENE AND COMPOSITION
Stage a recognizable vehicle-testing workshop from a slightly elevated, three-quarter front viewpoint. The raven stands in the left foreground. A small, elegant slate-teal vintage roadster occupies the center-right on a substantial charcoal rolling test stand. Three computer monitors hang above the rear workbench across the upper-left and upper-middle background.

The image should read immediately as “a skilled mechanic studying live measurements while an attractive car remains under controlled testing.” The raven’s upward gaze, the telemetry monitors, the electronic sensors, and the restrained wheels establish that relationship.

Give both the car and the testing operation substantial visual presence. The main subjects occupy roughly three quarters of the canvas, with clean breathing room around their silhouettes; secondary workshop furniture may extend toward the edges. Keep the raven’s inspection sheet, the copper adjustment handle, the sensor-to-car relationship, and the car’s wheels around the central band so a wide thumbnail crop retains the story.

RAVEN MECHANIC
Match the approved raven character: charcoal layered feather shapes, substantial slate-teal beak, off-white eyes with dark pupils, compact body, tapered tail, slender bird legs and toes, and wings that can grip objects through feather-like fingers.

Dress the raven as a modern Formula 1 team mechanic, not in an apron. Give it a fitted charcoal technical mechanic’s jumpsuit with light-gray inset panels, narrow burnt-copper stripes along the outer sleeves and trouser legs, practical seams, a simple belt, and one small utility pocket containing a wrench and an orange-handled tool. All clothing is made from layered matte paper. No branding, team names, sponsor patches, lettering, or helmet. Keep the feathered head, neck, wing tips, tail, and bird feet visible.

Show the raven in a three-quarter rear/side view, with its shoulders turned toward the wall monitors and its head tilted upward to study the middle screen. Keep the recognizable eye and beak visible in profile. Its gaze must clearly meet the monitor graphics rather than the car or the sheet in its wings.

The raven holds a large off-white inspection printout below its face, around chest-to-waist height, with feather-like fingers supporting the edges. Include only a small car silhouette, an illustrative line graph, broad document blocks, and a wheel diagram. The printout supports its comparison with the electronic results, but its attention is currently on the monitors. Its posture is attentive, analytical, and composed.

ROADSTER AND ROLLING TEST STAND
Make the roadster a compact, attractive classic convertible, with its front facing left and slightly toward the viewer. Give it rounded slate-teal bodywork, round pale headlights, a simple vertical grille, restrained light-gray trim, an open cockpit, a pale windshield frame, warm tan seats, dark tires, and layered spoke-like wheel hubs.

The car is stationary on a robust charcoal dynamometer-style test stand. Clearly show the tires resting between cylindrical rollers. Include substantial beams, triangular braces, visible paper-cut bolts, roller axles, and sturdy supports. Burnt-copper wheel restraints with charcoal brackets secure the visible front and rear wheels to the rig. Make the physical connection between car, rollers, restraints, and support frame unmistakable.

Retain a prominent burnt-copper adjustment handwheel with a short projecting grip on the upright near the car’s front-left corner. It belongs to the testing apparatus, not to the car.

LIVE TESTING MONITORS
Replace wall-mounted paper charts with exactly three modern flat-panel computer monitors in simple charcoal frames above the rear workbench. Their displays represent results from the roadster’s ongoing test.

Left monitor: a side-profile roadster silhouette, broad horizontal readout bars, and a small wheel diagram.
Middle monitor: two semicircular gauge arcs above a simple graph with teal and copper curves, plus a few vertical indicator bars.
Right monitor: a waveform plot beside an overhead axle-and-wheel schematic, with a few small status dots and abstract readout blocks.

Use layered paper lines and shapes for every interface element. The graphics are schematic visual shorthand, not real statistics or evidence. No words, numerals, scores, checkmarks, or pass/fail verdicts. Avoid neon, screen bloom, holograms, or colored light spilling onto the workshop.

ELECTRONIC TESTING APPARATUS
Make the sensors visibly contemporary and electronic, rather than a simple mechanical measuring arm. A sturdy vertical mast attached to the rig supports an articulated assembly of compact rectangular sensor housings, adjustment joints, and a precise measuring head positioned just above the roadster’s front bodywork.

Add a second compact sensor module near the rear wheel, mounted on its own support and aimed toward the vehicle. Connect the modules to the rig with a few neatly routed black cables, small copper connectors, and one short coiled lead. Include a compact control or acquisition box attached to the test stand and a single thicker conduit exiting the rig.

Use small matte indicator dots and simple panel details without text. Keep the electronics believable and orderly, with clear mounting points and purposeful connections. No floating devices, glowing scanning beams, or decorative circuitry.

WORKSHOP BACKGROUND
Keep the room tidy and functional. Beneath the monitors, show a muted teal workbench and drawer cabinet with a modest stack of inspection sheets, a small cup holding pencils or tools, and one simple sage-leaf plant in a muted copper-brown pot.

On the rear-right wall, include one compact charcoal tool board holding two wrenches and an orange-handled screwdriver. Place a closed sage-gray workshop door farther right, with a simple pale window panel and dark handle. A small portion of a rolling tool cabinet may appear at the far-right edge.

The background should establish a credible working environment without competing with the raven, screens, car, or test apparatus.

FINAL CONSTRAINTS
No readable text anywhere. No captions, logos, watermarks, actual statistics, or claims about performance. No victory, race finish, crashed vehicle, green release light, open exit, or car departing. The vehicle is an attractive candidate still being evaluated, not a proven success.

Avoid glossy materials, gradients, cinematic lighting, neon, holograms, robots, circuit-board decoration, excessive clutter, and a smooth 3D-render finish. Preserve the tactile matte-paper construction, clear visual hierarchy, and quiet whimsy throughout. One image only.

OUTPUT MASTER
Render a 1536x1024 landscape master; keep the decisive interaction in the center band for a later 16:9 crop.
